title: Maximal ideal equality after tame DVR base change
statement: Let $B$ and $A$ be DVR domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and give $A$ a finite faithful $B$-algebra structure. Let $n>0$ be a unit in $B$ and assume $\mathfrak m_B A=\mathfrak m_A^n$. Let $E/\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ be finite separable [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], with its composite $B$-algebra structure, and let $C=\operatorname{integralClosure}_B(E)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume for every prime $R$ of $C$ above $\mathfrak m_B$ that both its ramification index and residue degree divide $n$. For every maximal ideal $P$ of $D=E\otimes_B A$, give $F=D/P$ its $A$-algebra structure by the right tensor inclusion and put $S=\operatorname{integralClosure}_A(F)$. Assume $S$ is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For every prime ideal Q of S contracting to the maximal ideal of A, let S_Q be the localization at Q. The extension of the maximal ideal of A to S_Q equals the maximal ideal of S_Q.

source.place: Tags 032L (finite separable normalization), 0BRM (Abhyankar lemma), and 09E7 (adic smoothness of DVRs).

proof.text: Use Mathlib IsIntegralClosure.finite with the given finite-dimensional separable extension and the composite scalar tower to prove C finite over B.

Let beta:E -> F be the left tensor inclusion followed by the quotient. Tensor balancing identifies alpha composed with B -> A with beta composed with B -> E. The latter is injective, since it is a composite of field maps and the fraction-ring inclusion. Thus ker(alpha) contracts to zero in B. Mathlib Ideal.eq_bot_of_comap_eq_bot, using finiteness of A/B, makes the kernel zero, proving alpha injective.

Apply the quantitative tame ramification bound with r=n, the just-proved finiteness of C and injectivity of alpha, and the given finiteness of S. Since gcd(n,n)=n and n>0, the resulting index bound is Q.ramificationIdx A <= 1. Mathlib Ideal.ramificationIdx_pos gives positivity; hence the index is one.

Unfold Mathlib Ideal.ramificationIdx_def. ENat.toNat_eq_iff_eq_natCast at one gives quotient length one. Module.length_eq_one_iff gives a simple quotient module; isSimpleModule_iff_isCoatom and Ideal.isMaximal_def give maximality of the image of Q.under A in S_Q. IsLocalRing.isMaximal_iff identifies that image with m_(S_Q). Finally rewrite Q.under A using its definition and the assumed contraction equality to obtain exactly the claimed image of m_A.

proof_origin.place: Tags 032L and 0BRM; finite normalization and tensor-map injectivity proved directly in Lean, then quantitative bound and quotient-length criterion.

theorem dvr_tame_tensor_factor_map_maximalIdeal
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    (n : ℕ) (hnpos : 0 < n) (hn : IsUnit (n : B))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [Algebra B A] [Module.Finite B A] [FaithfulSMul B A]
    (hindex : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).map (algebraMap B A) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ^ n)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (FractionRing B) E]
    (hE : FiniteDimensional (FractionRing B) E ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing B) E) :
    letI : Algebra B E :=
      ((algebraMap (FractionRing B) E).comp (algebraMap B (FractionRing B))).toAlgebra
    let C := integralClosure B E
    (∀ (R : Ideal C) (hR : R.IsPrime),
      letI := hR
      R.comap (algebraMap B C) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B →
        R.ramificationIdx B ∣ n ∧ R.inertiaDeg B ∣ n) →
    let D := E ⊗[B] A
    ∀ (P : Ideal D) (hP : P.IsMaximal),
    let := hP
    let F := D ⧸ P
    let alpha : A →+* F := (Ideal.Quotient.mk P).comp
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : A →ₐ[B] D).toRingHom
    letI := alpha.toAlgebra
    let S := integralClosure A F
    Module.Finite A S →
    ∀ (Q : Ideal S) (hQ : Q.IsPrime),
    let := hQ
    Q.comap (algebraMap A S) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A →
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime Q)) =
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime Q)
